blog_summary: Adrian Colyer summarizes a critical analysis paper that challenges the Information Bottleneck (IB) theory of deep learning proposed by Schwartz-Viz & Tishby. The authors replicate the original findings but demonstrate that key results do not generalize across different network architectures, particularly when replacing tanh activations with ReLU. They show that the observed two-phase training dynamics (compression and fitting) depend heavily on the choice of activation function, with ReLU networks failing to exhibit compression. The paper further investigates the relationship between compression and generalization, finding no causal connection, and shows that compression is not dependent on randomness from SGD. The authors also explore task-irrelevant information compression, noting that while irrelevant information may compress, this does not necessarily correlate with generalization performance. Overall, the paper highlights limitations in applying information-theoretic analyses to deep learning systems, particularly regarding noise assumptions and activation function choices.
paper_title: Opening the Black Box: On the Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning
